meetings.title: Kickoff for the floor sensors at Halden Works
meetings.overview: The team kicked off the floor sensor rollout at Halden Works. Harlan leads and the first wave is small. The vendor and the schedule were agreed.
keyPoints: First wave is 40 sensors on line 4
decisions: Use glue-on mounts for all sensors
Harlan leads the rollout

actions.task: Draft the network plan for line 4
Get the gateway certified for the plant network

openQuestions: Where are the sensor readings stored?

say.text: Okay, welcome everyone. This is the kickoff for the floor sensor rollout at Halden Works. I will lead it.
The plan is 40 sensors on line 4, and we go live on Nov 4. The vendor is Tessaro Sensors.
I will own the network side. I need a plan for the gateways before anyone drills a hole.
And I own the press side. Press 7 is the noisy one, so I will start there.
How do we mount them? I would like glue-on mounts. They are fast and nobody has to drill the housings.
Glue is fine for a pilot. I ran a test on press 2 last week and it held for three days.
Fine by me. Let us write that down as the decision for now.
Next, the order. I will place the Tessaro order for 40 units this week.
Do we know where the readings are stored? I cannot size the network without that.
No. That is an open question. Put it on the list.
Operators will need training too. Somebody has to book the sessions.
I will take that. I will book the sessions before the end of the month.
The gateway needs a security certification before it can join the plant network. I will start that.
Alert limits come last, once we have a baseline. I will calibrate on press 7 for that.
Okay. Network plan by Oct 18, calibration by Oct 25. Let us meet again in two weeks.

meetings.title: Mounting problems and the network question
meetings.overview: The team reviewed the first mounting tests and the network options. The mounting approach changed after the pilot. Several earlier tasks are waiting on others.
keyPoints: Mounting method was revisited after the pilot
Wifi versus a wired link came up for the gateways
Gateway certification is still in progress
decisions: Switch from glue-on mounts to bolted brackets

actions.task: Draft the network plan for line 4
Place the order for 12 spare sensors
Get the gateway certified for line 4

openQuestions: Wifi or wired ethernet for the gateways?

say.text: Let us start with mounting. Cosmo, you said the glue held on press 2. What happened on press 7?
It failed. The press 7 housing runs at about 90 degrees Celsius near the die, and the glue softened in two days. Four sensors fell off.
So glue is dead for the hot presses. I propose bolted brackets for everything.
I agree. I can have 40 brackets cut this week.
Then I record the decision: bolted brackets replace glue.
Next, the network. I would like to look at wired ethernet instead of wifi for the gateways.
I am open to it, but wired means running cable. Let me price it.
Okay. Put it as an open question for now. What about the gateway certification, Mei-Lin?
It is stuck. I filed the firewall rules with IT security, ticket 4471, and they bounced it. They want the rules rewritten by port, not by subnet.
That costs us a week at least. Cosmo, thresholds?
Not started in earnest. I need real baseline data first, and the sensors are not even on the presses yet.
Right. About spares. We want 12 spare sensors because failures will happen.
I asked Tessaro. Their lead time on spares is nine weeks. That is a problem for the Nov 4 date.
Nine weeks is a long time. Can we get them from anywhere else?
Not now. I will keep the order open and chase them.
The network plan for line 4 is done, by the way. I saw Mei-Lin's draft.

meetings.title: Wired network push and calibration delay
meetings.overview: The team checked progress on installation and the network choice. Mei-Lin argued for a network change. Alert limits and training are slower than planned.
keyPoints: Installation on line 4 is partly done
decisions: Move the gateways in the welding area to wired ethernet

actions.task: Run ethernet cable to the welding bay

openQuestions: Who pays for storage of the readings?

say.text: Status check. The brackets are on, and 28 sensors are live on line 4. Twelve are waiting.
Before anything else I want to push on the network again. I want wired ethernet in the welding bay.
Mei-Lin, you proposed it last time as a question. Why is it so important now?
I measured it. Wifi dropped 31 percent of the packets near the welding bay. The arcs jam the signal.
That would wreck any alert work. I support wired.
Okay. Decision: gateways near the welding bay go wired. How long for the cable?
The run is 80 meters. I can finish by Nov 30 if the cable arrives.
Now the gateway certification. Status?
Good news and bad news. IT security accepted the rules, but the gateway needs firmware 2.8 to pass their scan. It ships Nov 19.
So we wait for the vendor. Cosmo, thresholds?
Behind. I only have six days of baseline data because press 7 was down for a die change. I need at least fourteen.
Understood. Training is also behind. Our trainer is on leave until Nov 25, so I cannot book anything.
Can anyone else train the operators?
Not with the safety sign-off. It has to be her.
The spare order is still open. Same story, I keep chasing Tessaro.

meetings.title: Second mounting change, power and customs
meetings.overview: The team reviewed field results from line 4 and the open blockers. The mounting method changed a second time. The gateway work and the spare order are still held up.
keyPoints: Mounting method changed again after field results
Spare sensors are still not here
Alerts depend on a data policy question
decisions: Use magnetic mounts on press housings and keep bolts on the conveyors

actions.task: Set vibration alert thresholds on press 7
Book training dates with the trainer
Replace bolts on press 7 with magnetic mounts

openQuestions: Who signs off the policy for shift data?

say.text: Field results first. Cosmo, how are the bolted brackets doing?
Not great on press 7. Vibration loosened the bolts twice in one week. Two sensors read garbage.
I propose magnetic mounts on the press housings. We keep bolts on the conveyors, where it is calm.
Magnets are fine for me. Same signal?
Same signal. I tested one for four days.
Okay, second change then. Magnetic on presses, bolts on conveyors. Record it.
The ethernet run to the welding bay is done. It works.
Good. Gateway certification, where are we?
Firmware 2.8 is in. The scan passes now. But the gateway cabinet needs a 24 volt rail, and the electrician is booked for Dec 3.
So the gateway waits for power. And the spares?
Tessaro shipped. The container is held at customs since Nov 17. No date yet.
Thresholds: I now have fourteen days of data. But the union asked for a review of the shift data policy before we turn on alerts. The review is set for Dec 10.
Alerts are the whole point. Who signs off?
HR and the union rep. I do not know who owns it.
We list that as an open question. The trainer is back Nov 25, so I will book Dec 12.

meetings.title: New scope, new vendor, new date
meetings.overview: The team reviewed the plan after the pilot and agreed a much bigger scope. The lead, the vendor and the schedule all differ from the kickoff. Some older items still wait on others.
keyPoints: Scope grew well beyond the pilot
A new go-live date was set
Storage cost is still not settled
decisions: Expand to 112 sensors across lines 4, 5 and 6
Replace Tessaro with Norvik
Cosmo takes over as lead

actions.task: Place the spare sensor order with Norvik
Replace bolts on press 7 with magnetic mounts

openQuestions: Which storage option wins, and under what retention period?

say.text: I am running this one. Harlan moved to the finance review, so I am the lead now.
Right, I stay around for the storage quote. Cosmo, give us the new plan.
Scope is now 112 sensors on lines 4, 5 and 6, up from 40. The new go-live is Jan 20.
And we dropped Tessaro. Norvik is the new vendor. Their lead time is three weeks, not nine.
That helps with spares. Why can we not order today?
The budget code for the spares is frozen until Jan 5. Finance closed the year.
OK, so the order waits. Mei-Lin, the gateway?
The electrician came on Dec 3 and the power is in. It is a short sign-off now. I expect Jan 8.
Thresholds: I run alerts in test mode only, for now.
Training is blocked on the room. The safety audit takes the training room the week of Jan 12.
Quick one on storage. IT quoted 5,800 a month for on-site. A cloud option came in at 4,100.
So cloud wins?
Not yet. Legal has not said how long we must keep the readings. Seven years or ninety days changes the price a lot.
When will legal answer?
They promised Jan 19. Until then storage is unsettled.
Okay. Same list as last time, just with new dates. We meet again after the holiday.

meetings.title: Início da plataforma de doações da Casa Girassol
meetings.overview: A equipe abriu o projeto da plataforma de doações da Casa Girassol. Valdemar coordena e Anselmo cuida da parte técnica. A meta e a data de lançamento foram definidas.
keyPoints: Meta de arrecadação mensal definida em R$ 18 mil
Provedor de pagamento escolhido: Tapioca Pay
decisions: Aceitar apenas Pix no início
Usar a Tapioca Pay como provedor

actions.task: Criar o cadastro na Tapioca Pay
Redigir o termo de consentimento LGPD

openQuestions: Como os doadores recebem o recibo?

say.text: Bom dia, pessoal. Vamos começar a plataforma de doações da Casa Girassol. Eu coordeno o projeto.
A meta é arrecadar 18 mil reais por mês. A gente lança no dia 12 de março.
Eu cuido da parte técnica. Já escolhi o provedor: a Tapioca Pay. A taxa deles é boa.
Eu cuido do financeiro e dos recibos. Doador de ONG quer recibo para abater imposto.
Verdade. Consegue emitir recibo fiscal automático?
Consigo, mas preciso de algumas coisas da prefeitura. Vou ver o que falta.
Anselmo, quais formas de pagamento a gente aceita no começo?
Eu sugiro só Pix. É simples, é barato e todo mundo tem.
Para mim está bom. Só Pix no começo.
E o termo de consentimento? Pela LGPD a gente precisa de um texto para os dados dos doadores.
Esse eu mesmo redijo e mando para o jurídico.
Vou criar o cadastro na Tapioca Pay amanhã e depois desenho a página de doação.
Ótimo. Quando fica pronto o primeiro teste?
Em umas duas semanas, se nada travar.
Combinado. A gente se fala de novo no fim do mês.

meetings.title: Cartão e recibos
meetings.overview: A equipe revisou o andamento da página de doação e discutiu novas formas de pagamento. A emissão de recibos ficou parada. Uma ideia para o modelo de doação apareceu.
keyPoints: Ideia de mudança no modelo de doação
decisions: Adicionar cartão de crédito além do Pix

actions.task: Redigir o termo de consentimento LGPD
Criar o cadastro na Tapioca Pay

say.text: Vamos ao andamento. Anselmo, como está a página?
Quase pronta. Falta ligar o botão do Pix no ambiente de teste.
Eu recebi pedidos de doadores que querem pagar no cartão. Podemos aceitar?
Dá. A Tapioca Pay já tem cartão. Leva uns cinco dias de trabalho.
Então decidido: Pix e cartão de crédito.
Tenho uma proposta também. Queria falar de doação mensal, mas deixo para depois.
Fica como pergunta em aberto. E os recibos, Yasmin?
Parados. O certificado digital da ONG venceu no dia 15 de janeiro. Sem ele a prefeitura não aceita a emissão.
Quanto custa renovar?
Uns 240 reais, mas a emissão leva de cinco a dez dias.
Eu posso ajudar com a instalação do certificado quando chegar.
Ok. Yasmin, vê isso ainda hoje.
Vou ver. E o termo de LGPD, Valdemar?
Ainda não terminei. Vou mandar para o jurídico semana que vem.
Então a gente fecha por aqui. Próxima em duas semanas.

meetings.title: Doação recorrente e cadastro
meetings.overview: A equipe discutiu o modelo de doações e o andamento dos recibos. Uma mudança no uso do cartão foi acertada. Outros bloqueios apareceram nas conversas.
keyPoints: Cartão passa a ter uso mais restrito
Recibos seguem parados por outro motivo
decisions: Cartão só para doação mensal recorrente e Pix para doação única

actions.task: Corrigir o cadastro de atividade da ONG
Cobrar o parecer do jurídico sobre o termo

openQuestions: Qual é a data real de lançamento?

say.text: Primeiro assunto: doação recorrente. Yasmin, você queria falar disso.
Queria sim, e agora tenho os números. Em 2023, 73 por cento das doações vieram em dezembro. De fevereiro a abril a ONG fica sem caixa.
Com doação mensal a gente forma uma base fixa. Eu defendo que o cartão seja só para recorrência.
Faz sentido técnico. Cartão para recorrência é mais simples de cobrar.
Então eu decido: cartão só para doação mensal recorrente, e Pix para doação única.
Isso aumenta o trabalho. Preciso de umas três semanas a mais.
Tudo bem. E os recibos? O certificado chegou?
Chegou e instalamos. Mas agora travou em outra coisa: o contador disse que o CNAE da ONG está errado no cadastro.
Com o CNAE errado a prefeitura rejeita o pedido. Tenho que pedir a correção na Receita.
Quanto tempo?
Uns quinze dias, no mínimo.
O termo de LGPD já está escrito. Mandei para o jurídico faz uma semana e não voltou.
Sem o parecer a gente não pode abrir o formulário de dados.
Eu cobro. Então a data de 12 de março está difícil.
Com certeza. Eu estimo abril.
Ok, a gente reavalia na próxima.

meetings.title: Nova data e prefeitura
meetings.overview: A equipe fez o balanço e fixou uma nova data de lançamento. A coordenação mudou de mãos. Os recibos e o termo ainda dependem de terceiros.
decisions: Trocar a Tapioca Pay pela Zepay
Lançar em 28 de abril

actions.task: Cobrar o parecer do jurídico sobre o termo
Migrar o cadastro para a Zepay
Fazer teste de Pix com valor real

openQuestions: O parecer do jurídico chega antes do lançamento?

say.text: Eu coordeno daqui para a frente. O Valdemar foi para a captação de recursos.
Isso. Eu fico nos doadores grandes. Apresenta a situação.
Meta nova: 42 mil reais por mês, porque dois patrocinadores fecharam. A data de lançamento passou para 28 de abril.
Também trocamos o provedor. Saímos da Tapioca Pay e vamos para a Zepay. A taxa de cartão é menor, e eles fazem recorrência nativa.
Quanto isso muda no cronograma?
Uma semana de migração. O resto fica igual.
Recibos: o CNAE foi corrigido, mas agora o sistema da prefeitura está fora do ar até 15 de abril por causa de uma migração.
Então os recibos só saem depois disso.
Sim. Dá tempo, mas por pouco.
Quero fazer um teste de Pix com valor real antes do lançamento.
Combinado. Dia 18 de abril.
E o parecer do jurídico sobre o termo de LGPD?
Eles prometeram para 10 de abril. Mas já prometeram duas vezes.
Se não vier, lançamos sem o formulário completo?
Não. Sem parecer a gente não lança. É a decisão da coordenação.
Ok. Então a data de 28 de abril depende dessa resposta.

meetings.title: Loyalty and pricing kickoff
meetings.overview: The team opened the loyalty and pricing rework for Dunmore Grocers. Cosmo leads, with a small pilot first. The loyalty structure and the launch date were set.
keyPoints: Loyalty program starts with three tiers
Budget of 120k approved by the board
Members log in with an app account
decisions: Run the pilot in six stores
Launch loyalty with three tiers: Bronze, Silver and Gold

actions.task: Write the price match policy for dairy
Get a quote for electronic shelf labels

openQuestions: How long do points stay valid?

say.text: Okay, let us start. I lead this rework, loyalty and pricing together. The pilot is six stores, and we launch on Apr 15.
And the budget for the pilot?
It is 120k, approved by the board.
I run store operations, so anything on the floor goes through me. That includes the shelf labels.
I own pricing. I want to talk about how often we change shelf prices, but later.
First the loyalty structure. I propose three tiers: Bronze, Silver, Gold. Gold gets the best coupons.
Three tiers is the standard. I am fine with that.
Staff will need to explain it at the till. Three is a lot, but okay.
Members log in with an app account. No account, no points.
Many older customers do not use the app. Let us note that as a risk.
Noted. Ruth, what about the shelf labels?
Electronic labels would let us change prices in minutes. I will get a quote.
Also, we need a price match policy for dairy. Customers keep asking.
I will pull twelve months of basket data first, so everything rests on facts.
And points expiry and coupon expiry need rules. Who writes them?
I take points expiry. Lucinda takes coupons.
Good. We meet in two weeks.

meetings.title: Tiers shrink, labels hit a wall
meetings.overview: The team reviewed early basket data and the tier design. The loyalty structure changed after the data came in. The label rollout hit its first hurdle.
keyPoints: Basket data changed the tier discussion
A faster price rhythm was floated
decisions: Cut the program from three tiers to two tiers

actions.task: Draft the expiry rules for points
Plan the electronic shelf label pilot in store 12

openQuestions: Should prices change weekly instead of monthly?

say.text: The basket data is in. Only 9 percent of members ever reach Gold, so Gold barely matters.
I propose two tiers: Member and Plus. It is simpler for the till staff.
That works for me. Fewer tiers, fewer coupon variants.
Staff will like it. I agree.
Decision: two tiers instead of three.
Now the pricing rhythm. I want to try changing key prices weekly, not monthly. Let me raise it as a question.
We will come back to it. Ruth, the labels?
Store 12 is the pilot store. The survey showed dead zones across the back half of the store. The labels talk over wifi and cannot reach.
How many aisles?
Seven of eleven. We would need extra access points.
That is extra cost. How much?
About 14 thousand for that store. I do not have approval.
The quote for the labels is in?
Yes. The per label price is fine. The infrastructure is the issue.
The dairy matching policy, I still have no draft.
Same for the points rules. Both slip to next time.

meetings.title: Weekly pricing and label batteries
meetings.overview: The team looked at pricing frequency and the label test results. A change of rhythm was agreed. The labels remain a problem.
keyPoints: Coupon and expiry rules still not written
Dairy matching question pending outside advice
decisions: Update key prices weekly

actions.task: Write the price match policy for dairy
Build the weekly price update job
Run the electronic shelf label pilot in store 12

openQuestions: Does the dairy price match break a pricing rule?

say.text: I need to push for weekly price changes. Last time I only raised it.
Lucinda, why does it matter this much?
A discounter across the road changes dairy prices every Tuesday. We lost 6 percent of dairy baskets in January because we were a week behind.
That is a real number. I am in. Weekly it is, for key items.
Weekly needs the labels to work, otherwise my staff print paper tags.
Then labels. Ruth, the battery test?
Bad news. The supplier says five years of battery life. In our cold aisle test, the labels died in 14 months of simulated use.
That is not usable for dairy. The cold aisle is where we need them.
The supplier offered a new battery pack, but it ships in six weeks.
I will build the weekly price job. It does not need the labels.
Coupon expiry rules are still not written. Sorry.
Same on points expiry. I have not started.
And for the dairy price match, I think it might clash with a state pricing rule. I asked outside counsel.
Fine. We keep that open.
One more thing. Store managers are nervous about changes before spring.
Noted. We discuss it next time.

meetings.title: Wider rollout and a new lead
meetings.overview: The team reviewed pilot results and agreed a much larger rollout. The lead, the scope and the launch date all differ from the start. Some questions remain open.
decisions: Move to a single tier with a points multiplier
Pause the electronic label rollout
Launch Jun 3 in 31 stores

actions.task: Write the price match policy for dairy
Build the weekly price update job
Rework store training for one tier

openQuestions: Can the dairy price match go live in all 31 stores?

say.text: I lead the rollout from today. Cosmo moved to the data platform team.
Right. Short version for the record: we go from six stores to 31 stores, and the budget is 310k now.
Launch moves from Apr 15 to Jun 3.
And loyalty is down to one tier now. Everyone earns points, and Plus members get a multiplier.
The two tiers still confused the till staff. One tier with a multiplier is the simplest.
Agreed. Training gets easier too.
Weekly prices run. The job is done.
Yes, the job runs every Monday night.
Labels: I have to pause. Store managers asked us to wait until after the spring inventory count, because the count crews need the old tags.
So no labels in the first wave.
Right. Paper tags for weekly changes in the first wave.
The dairy price match is still unsettled. The attorney general's office promised an opinion by Mar 22, but it has not arrived.
Until then we cannot publish the policy.
And coupon and points expiry? Still not written.
My bad. Both are due next month.
Okay. Ruth owns the list from now on.
